claim: 58% of changed transcripts during MEF-to-iN cell reprogramming corresponded to non-coding genes while only 42% corresponded to coding genes.
source: Specifically, 58% of the changed transcripts corresponded to non-coding genes while only 42% of them corresponded to coding genes.
evidence: Based on annotation of the iN cell reprogramming transcriptome and quantitative analysis presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: About two thirds of non-coding transcripts during iN cell reprogramming were composed of novel lncRNAs.
source: About two thirds of these non-coding transcripts were composed of novel lncRNAs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Quantitative analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 287 non-coding transcripts significantly changed expression during MEF-to-iN cell reprogramming time course (RPKM >1, fold change >2, p-value<0.05).
source: We observed 287 non-coding transcripts significantly changed expression during this time course (RPKM >1, fold change >2, p-value<0.05) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Statistical analysis of RNA-seq data with specified thresholds.

claim: LncRNAs that increased expression during early stages of iN cell reprogramming are more highly expressed in embryonic mouse brain, specifically in ventricular and subventricular zones where neurogenesis occurs.
source: Notably, lncRNAs that increased expression during early stages of iN cell reprogramming are more highly expressed in embryonic mouse brain, specifically in ventricular and subventricular zones where neurogenesis occurs; whereas lncRNAs that increased expression during intermediate to late stages of iN cell reprogramming were more highly expressed in adult mouse brain, including in mature cortical layers (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: Expression pattern analysis across developmental stages shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: LncRNAs that increased expression during intermediate to late stages of iN cell reprogramming were more highly expressed in adult mouse brain, including in mature cortical layers.
source: Notably, lncRNAs that increased expression during early stages of iN cell reprogramming are more highly expressed in embryonic mouse brain, specifically in ventricular and subventricular zones where neurogenesis occurs; whereas lncRNAs that increased expression during intermediate to late stages of iN cell reprogramming were more highly expressed in adult mouse brain, including in mature cortical layers (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: Expression pattern analysis across developmental stages shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: Some of the 287 iN lncRNAs are chromatin-associated compared to IgG control and input in neural precursor cells (NPCs) or adult mouse brain tissue.
source: We performed histone H3 immunoprecipitation, followed by deep sequencing of associated RNAs (histone H3 RIP-seq), and discovered some of these 287 iN lncRNAs are chromatin-associated compared to IgG control and input in neural precursor cells (NPCs) or adult mouse brain tissue, suggesting that some of them may have more direct roles in gene expression control at the chromatin (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Histone H3 RIP-seq experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: One predominant module of lncRNAs was strongly associated with neuronal GO terms, such as neurogenesis, axonogenesis, and synaptic organization and biogenesis.
source: Among the three predominant modules found, one was strongly associated with neuronal GO terms, such as neurogenesis, axonogenesis, and synaptic organization and biogenesis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Co-expression analysis and Gene Ontology enrichment shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: 35 iN cell lncRNAs were nominated as most promising for possessing functions in the brain based on the filtering pipeline.
source: Based on the criteria included in the pipeline, we nominated 35 iN cell lncRNAs as most promising for possessing functions in the brain and confirmed their expression qRT-PCR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Pipeline filtering and qRT-PCR validation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: 28 of the 35 mouse lncRNA candidates have human synteny.
source: Firstly, we found that 28 of the 35 mouse lncRNA candidates have human synteny, and 10 loci were already annotated as non-coding RNAs (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Synteny analysis comparing mouse and human genomes.

claim: 10 loci of the 35 mouse lncRNA candidates were already annotated as non-coding RNAs.
source: Firstly, we found that 28 of the 35 mouse lncRNA candidates have human synteny, and 10 loci were already annotated as non-coding RNAs (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Annotation analysis of lncRNA loci.

claim: The CNV morbidity map was built from 29,085 patients diagnosed with a spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders and craniofacial congenital malformations, and 19,584 controls.
source: We next overlapped the 28 human lncRNA candidates and the remaining iN cell-lncRNAs coordinates to a CNV morbidity map recently built from 29,085 patients diagnosed with a spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders and craniofacial congenital malformations, and 19,584 controls (Coe et al., 2014; Cooper et al., 2011).
evidence: Citation to published CNV morbidity map studies.

claim: The CNV morbidity map has successfully identified novel syndromes characterized by recurrent mutations affecting protein-coding genes of ASD/ID patients.
source: This approach was motivated by the fact that the CNV morbidity map has successfully identified novel syndromes characterized by recurrent mutations affecting protein-coding genes of ASD/ID patients, and has offered mechanistic insight into the drivers of the pathogenesis (Coe et al., 2014; Cooper et al., 2011; Turner et al., 2017).
evidence: Citation to published studies demonstrating utility of CNV morbidity map.

claim: Seven focal CNVs enriched in disease overlap with five candidate lncRNA loci: E (FLJ42709), H (LOC339529), Z (LOC100630918), D (LINC00094) and O (LOC467979).
source: Intersecting genomic coordinates of human lncRNA candidate loci to the CNV morbidity map revealed seven focal CNVs enriched in disease that overlap with five candidate lncRNA loci: E (FLJ42709), H (LOC339529), Z (LOC100630918), D (LINC00094) and O (LOC467979) (Sequences in supplementary documents).
evidence: Computational intersection of genomic coordinates with CNV morbidity map.

claim: Among the seven focal CNVs, five events corresponded to small deletions in human lncRNA candidates E, H, Z, D and O.
source: Among these seven focal CNVs, five events corresponded to small deletions in human lncRNA candidates E, H, Z, D and O.
evidence: Analysis of CNV types affecting lncRNA loci.

claim: 5 of 7 focal CNVs affecting the lncRNA loci were validated by custom tilling array CGH.
source: We then designed a custom tilling array with dense coverage of the affected loci for comparative genomic hybridization (CGH) to validate the focal CNVs in the genomic DNA from affected individuals. 5 of 7 focal CNVs affecting the lncRNA loci were tested and validated (Figure 1A and B, Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: CGH array validation experiments shown in Figure 1A, B and Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: The lncRNA locus NR_033883 (LOC339529) is disrupted by two focal CNVs in two distinct ASD/ID patients: 990914 and 9900589.
source: One of the focally deleted lncRNA was NR_033883 (also known as or LOC339529). This lncRNA locus is disrupted by two focal CNVs in two distinct ASD/ID patients: 990914 and 9900589 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: CNV analysis and CGH validation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: The human NR_033883 locus is most proximal but does not overlap ZFP238.
source: Because the human NR_033883 locus is most proximal but does not overlap ZFP238, we propose to refer to this lncRNA as lnc-ZFP238.
evidence: Genomic location analysis of lncRNA relative to nearby coding gene.

claim: ZFP238 was previously identified as a key downstream target of the Ascl1 network during MEF to iN cell reprogramming.
source: Intriguingly, we previously identified ZFP238 as a key downstream target of the Ascl1 network during MEF to iN cell reprogramming (Wapinski et al., 2013).
evidence: Citation to previous study by the authors.

claim: ZFP238 has an important role in neuronal differentiation during brain development.
source: Additionally, ZFP238 has an important role in neuronal differentiation during brain development (Xiang et al., 2012; Ohtaka-Maruyama et al., 2013; Baubet et al., 2012), and thus, lnc-ZFP238 could have a promising neurogenic role given its high expression pattern during the early stages of direct neuronal reprogramming, as well as in postnatal mouse and human brain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Citations to published studies on ZFP238 function.

claim: The locus harboring human FLJ42709 (or NR2F1-AS1) is focally deleted and is adjacent to the protein-coding gene NR2F1.
source: Another focally deleted lncRNA was the locus harboring human FLJ42709 (or NR2F1-AS1) (Figure 1B) which is adjacent to the protein-coding gene NR2F1 (also known as COUP-TF1), encoding a transcription factor involved in neurogenesis and patterning (Ramos et al., 2013; Armentano et al., 2006; Borello et al., 2014; Faedo et al., 2008; Harrison-Uy et al., 2013; Lin et al., 2011; Job and Tan, 2003; Tsai and Tsai, 1997; O'Leary et al., 2007).
evidence: CNV analysis shown in Figure 1B and citations to NR2F1 function studies.

claim: NR2F1 encodes a transcription factor involved in neurogenesis and patterning.
source: Another focally deleted lncRNA was the locus harboring human FLJ42709 (or NR2F1-AS1) (Figure 1B) which is adjacent to the protein-coding gene NR2F1 (also known as COUP-TF1), encoding a transcription factor involved in neurogenesis and patterning (Ramos et al., 2013; Armentano et al., 2006; Borello et al., 2014; Faedo et al., 2008; Harrison-Uy et al., 2013; Lin et al., 2011; Job and Tan, 2003; Tsai and Tsai, 1997; O'Leary et al., 2007).
evidence: Citations to published studies on NR2F1 function.

claim: At least one isoform of the mouse lncRNA and all detected isoforms of the human lncRNA are transcribed divergently from NR2F1 without antisense overlap.
source: However, our RNA-seq analysis showed that at least one isoform of the mouse lncRNA and all detected isoform of the human lncRNA are transcribed divergently from NR2F1 without antisense overlap (Ramos et al., 2013).
evidence: RNA-seq analysis of transcript structure and citation to supporting study.

claim: The focal deletion found in patient 9900850 disrupts only the lnc-NR2F1 locus.
source: Moreover, we precisely mapped the independent focal deletion found in patient 9900850 by CGH analysis and found only the lnc-NR2F1 locus to be disrupted (Figure 1B).
evidence: CGH analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A patient (CMS12200) harbors a paternally inherited balanced translocation t(5;12) (q15;q15).
source: Independent of the patients previously reported (Al-Kateb et al., 2013; Brown et al., 2009; Cardoso et al., 2009; Malan et al., 2006), we identified a paternally inherited balanced translocation t(5;12) (q15;q15) in a 2 year and 7-month-old male patient (CMS12200) (Figure 1C–D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: Genetic analysis shown in Figure 1C-D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Patient CMS12200 was diagnosed with developmental delay, speech delay, significant expressive language delay, and congenital infantile left eye esotropia.
source: Patient CMS12200 was diagnosed with developmental delay, speech delay, significant expressive language delay, and congenital infantile left eye esotropia (Figure 1C).
evidence: Clinical diagnosis information presented in Figure 1C.

claim: Physical examination of patient CMS12200 revealed small head size (head circumference 48.5 cm; fifth-tenth centile), and mild fifth finger clinodactyly bilaterally.
source: Physical examination revealed small head size (head circumference 48.5 cm; fifth-tenth centile), and mild fifth finger clinodactyly bilaterally.
evidence: Clinical examination data.

claim: The patient's father was diagnosed with dyslexia and stutters, and carried the identical t(5;12) translocation.
source: The patient's father was diagnosed with dyslexia and stutters, and carried the identical t(5;12) translocation.
evidence: Clinical and genetic information from family pedigree analysis.

claim: The patient's mother had a normal 46, XX karyotype.
source: The patient's mother had a normal 46, XX karyotype (Figure 1C).
evidence: Karyotype analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Fluorescence in situ hybridization and whole genome sequencing defined the chromosomal breakpoints with high precision and revealed that only the lnc-NR2F1 gene is disrupted in patient CMS12200.
source: Fluorescence in situ hybridization and whole genome sequencing defined the chromosomal breakpoints with high precision and revealed that only the lnc-NR2F1 gene is disrupted in this patient (Figure 1D and E, Figure 1—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: FISH and whole genome sequencing data shown in Figure 1D, E and Figure 1—figure supplement 4C.

claim: The long isoforms (1 and 2) of human lnc-NR2F1 are affected by the chromosomal break in patient CMS12200, while the gene structure of the short isoform (3) could remain unaffected based on the location of the break.
source: In humans, three predominant isoforms of lnc-NR2F1 have been detected in neuronal tissue. The long isoforms (1 and 2) are affected by the chromosomal break, while the gene structure of the short isoform (3) could remain unaffected based on the location of the break (Figure 1D).
evidence: Analysis of isoform structure relative to breakpoint shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Sanger sequencing of the breakpoint-specific junction fragments showed a loss of 9 nucleotides at the 5q15 chromosome and a loss of 12 nucleotides at the 12q15 chromosome in the patient and his father.
source: Further studies by Sanger sequencing of the 5q15 and 12q15 breakpoint-specific junction fragments showed the identical breakpoints in the patient's father and revealed a loss of 9 nucleotides at the 5q15 chromosome and a loss of 12 nucleotides at the 12q15 chromosome in the patient and his father (Figure 1D).
evidence: Sanger sequencing data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The breakpoint at 12q15 occurred in a coding gene desert and did not disrupt any coding genes.
source: The breakpoint at 12q15 occurred in a coding gene desert and did not disrupt any coding genes, and is predicted to destabilize the affected transcript due to loss of 3' splice or polyadenylation signals (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4D–E).
evidence: Genomic analysis of breakpoint location shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4D-E.

claim: Whole genome sequencing data indicated the absence of other deleterious mutations known to be associated with autism or intellectual disability in patient CMS12200.
source: Importantly, whole genome sequencing data indicated the absence of other deleterious mutations known to be associated with autism or intellectual disability, to our knowledge (Figure 1D).
evidence: Whole genome sequencing analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Lnc-NR2F1 is not only syntenically conserved in its genomic context but also highly sequence conserved among all human lnc-NR2F1 isoforms and the three exons in mouse lnc-Nr2f1.
source: Remarkably, and in contrast to many other lncRNAs, lnc-Nr2f1 was not only syntenically conserved in its genomic context (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, Supplementary file 6) (Quinn et al., 2016), but also highly sequence conserved among all human lnc-NR2F1 isoforms and the three exons in mouse lnc-Nr2f1 (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Synteny and sequence conservation analysis shown in Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-B, and Supplementary file 6.

claim: Short stretches of sequence homology (termed microhomology) near the conserved exons (exon 2 and 3 of human lnc-NR2F1) exist across different species, with recurrent sequence motifs and motif order conserved across different species.
source: In addition, we identified short stretches of sequence homology (termed microhomology) near the conserved exons (exon 2 and 3 of human lnc-NR2F1) across different species, with recurrent sequence motifs and motif order conserved across different species (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Sequence analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Mouse lnc-Nr2f1 is induced as early as 48 hr after BAM factors are expressed during MEF-to-iN cell conversion and peaks during mid-to-late stages of reprogramming.
source: Mouse lnc-Nr2f1 is induced as early as 48 hr after BAM factors are expressed during MEF-to-iN cell conversion and peaks during mid-to-late stages of reprogramming (Figure 2B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Expression time course data shown in Figure 2B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In the developing telencephalon at E13.5, in situ hybridization with a probe against lnc-Nr2f1 revealed strong expression in the caudolateral part of the mouse cortex and ganglionic eminences (GE), similar to Nr2f1 expression.
source: In the developing telencephalon at E13.5, in situ hybridization with a probe against lnc-Nr2f1 revealed strong expression in the caudolateral part of the mouse cortex and ganglionic eminences (GE), similar to Nr2f1 expression (Jonk et al., 1994) (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: In situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B, with citation to Nr2f1 expression pattern.

claim: Single molecule RNA-FISH in MEFs ectopically expressing lnc-Nr2f1 revealed a nuclear and cytoplasmic but predominantly nuclear localization.
source: To determine lnc-Nr2f1's cellular localization, we performed single molecule RNA-FISH in MEFs ectopically expressing lnc-Nr2f1, which revealed a nuclear and cytoplasmic but predominantly nuclear localization (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Single molecule RNA-FISH data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Cellular fractionation from primary neurons dissected from caudal region of the cortex showed endogenous localization of lnc-Nr2f1 in both nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions.
source: Consistently, cellular fractionation from primary neurons dissected from caudal region of the cortex showed endogenous localization of lnc-Nr2f1 in both nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions (Figure 2E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–I).
evidence: Cellular fractionation data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1H-I.

claim: Within the nuclear fraction, lnc-Nr2f1 is enriched in chromatin as assayed by histone H3 RNA Immunoprecipitation followed by qRT-PCR in brain-derived NPCs, postnatal and adult mouse brain.
source: Within the nuclear fraction, lnc-Nr2f1 is enriched in chromatin as assayed by histone H3 RNA Immunoprecipitation followed by qRT-PCR (histone H3 RIP-qRT-PCR) in brain-derived NPCs, postnatal and adult mouse brain (Figure 2F).
evidence: Histone H3 RIP-qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The addition of lnc-Nr2f1 with Ascl1 showed an approximately 50% (1.5-fold) significant increase in the number of TauEGFP positive cells with neurites relative to Ascl1 alone at day 7.
source: Indeed, the addition of lnc-Nr2f1 showed an approximately 50% (1.5-fold) significant increase in the number of TauEGFP positive cells with neurites relative to Ascl1 alone (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: Quantification of neuronal morphology shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: RNA-seq in sorted 7d MEF-iN cells expressing Ascl1, with and without co-expression of lnc-Nr2f1, revealed 343 genes significantly changed expression (RPKM >1, FDR corrected p<0.001).
source: RNA-seq in sorted 7d MEF-iN cells expressing Ascl1, with and without co-expression of lnc-Nr2f1, revealed 343 genes significantly changed expression between data sets (RPKM >1, FDR corrected p<0.001) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and E).
evidence: RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and E.

claim: The vast majority of genes changed by lnc-Nr2f1 expression were induced, with 311 genes up- and 32 down-regulated.
source: The vast majority of these genes were induced in expression upon lnc-Nr2f1 expression, with 311 genes up- and 32 down-regulated, suggesting lnc-Nr2f1 may positively enhance transcription.
evidence: RNA-seq analysis showing directional changes in gene expression.

claim: Gene ontology (GO) term enrichment of up regulated genes upon lnc-Nr2f1 expression showed significant enrichment in biological functions related to plasma membrane and neuronal function.
source: Gene ontology (GO) term enrichment of up regulated genes showed significant enrichment in biological functions related to plasma membrane (extracellular region, cell adhesion, and transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase activity) and neuronal function (neuron projection, calcium binding, neuron differentiation, and axonogenesis) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Overexpression of lnc-Nr2f1 in mES cells together with Ngn2 showed a significant increase in neurite length though the number of neurons remained the same.
source: Consistent with the fibroblast reprogramming results, we saw a significant increase in neurite length upon lnc-Nr2f1 overexpression though the number of neurons remained the same (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Neurite length and neuron count quantification shown in Figure 3B-D.

claim: Overexpression of the coding gene Nr2f1 did not induce neuronal maturation phenotypes, and instead caused a drastic reduction in the number of neurons.
source: In contrast, overexpression of the coding gene Nr2f1 did not induce these phenotypes, and instead caused a drastic reduction in the number of neurons (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Neurite length and neuron count quantification shown in Figure 3B-D.

claim: RNA-seq analysis showed lnc-Nr2f1 overexpression led to the induction of genes with functions in axon guidance and neuronal projection development (FDR corrected p<0.10, fold change >1.5).
source: RNA-seq analysis showed lnc-Nr2f1 overexpression led to the induction of genes with functions in axon guidance (Sema5d, Epha1) and neuronal projection development (Tubb6, Stmn2, Dtnbp1) (Figure 3E), confirming the cell biology phenotype (FDR corrected p<0.10, fold change >1.5).
evidence: RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 3E with specified statistical thresholds.

claim: RNA-seq showed that 348 genes were differentially expressed between the control and the lnc-Nr2f1 KO neurons, which can be subsequently rescued with lnc-Nr2f1 overexpression (FDR corrected p<0.10).
source: RNA-seq showed that 348 genes were differentially expressed between the control and the lnc-Nr2f1 KO neurons, which can be subsequently rescued with lnc-Nr2f1 overexpression (FDR corrected p<0.10) (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F with specified statistical threshold.

claim: Lnc-Nr2f1 KO led to down regulation of neuronal pathfinding and axon guidance genes such as Sema6d and proneural bHLH transcription factor Neurod2.
source: Consistent with target genes in our lnc-Nr2f1 overexpression study, we found lnc-Nr2f1 KO led to down regulation of neuronal pathfinding and axon guidance genes such as Sema6d and proneural bHLH transcription factor Neurod2 as well as deregulation of genes associated with autism spectrum disorder such as Bdnf, Dcx and Nlgn3 (Basu et al., 2009) (Figure 3G).
evidence: RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 3G with citation to autism gene database.

claim: Lnc-Nr2f1 KO led to deregulation of genes associated with autism spectrum disorder such as Bdnf, Dcx and Nlgn3.
source: Consistent with target genes in our lnc-Nr2f1 overexpression study, we found lnc-Nr2f1 KO led to down regulation of neuronal pathfinding and axon guidance genes such as Sema6d and proneural bHLH transcription factor Neurod2 as well as deregulation of genes associated with autism spectrum disorder such as Bdnf, Dcx and Nlgn3 (Basu et al., 2009) (Figure 3G).
evidence: RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 3G with citation to autism gene database.

claim: The transcriptional abnormalities in lnc-Nr2f1 KO were reversed by enforced expression of lnc-Nr2f1 from a heterologous construct via lentiviral transduction.
source: The transcriptional abnormalities were reversed by enforced expression of lnc-Nr2f1 from a heterologous construct via lentiviral transduction.
evidence: Rescue experiment demonstrating reversibility of phenotype.

claim: Gene Ontology analysis of the downregulated genes in lnc-Nr2f1 KO neurons revealed enrichment for terms related to neural functions (regionalization, central nervous system development and neural precursor cell proliferation).
source: Gene Ontology analysis of the downregulated genes in lnc-Nr2f1 KO neurons revealed enrichment for terms related to neural functions (regionalization, central nervous system development and neural precursor cell proliferation), whereas the upregulated genes are enriched in development of non-neuronal tissues such as circulatory system and skin development (Figure 3H and I).
evidence: Gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 3H and I.

claim: The upregulated genes in lnc-Nr2f1 KO neurons are enriched in development of non-neuronal tissues such as circulatory system and skin development.
source: Gene Ontology analysis of the downregulated genes in lnc-Nr2f1 KO neurons revealed enrichment for terms related to neural functions (regionalization, central nervous system development and neural precursor cell proliferation), whereas the upregulated genes are enriched in development of non-neuronal tissues such as circulatory system and skin development (Figure 3H and I).
evidence: Gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 3H and I.

claim: The rescued genes overlap significantly with curated autism risk genes (p=0.0012, Chi-square).
source: Finally, the rescued genes overlap significantly with curated autism risk genes by Basu et. al. (Basu et al., 2009) (p=0.0012, Chi-square) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Statistical overlap analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G with citation to autism gene database.

claim: Nr2f1 KO did not affect lnc-Nr2f1 expression.
source: The Nr2f1 KO did not affect lnc-Nr2f1 expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B) and had no impact on the neurite length or number in mES-iN cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D–E).
evidence: qRT-PCR and morphological analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, D-E.

claim: Nr2f1 KO had no impact on the neurite length or number in mES-iN cells.
source: The Nr2f1 KO did not affect lnc-Nr2f1 expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B) and had no impact on the neurite length or number in mES-iN cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D–E).
evidence: Morphological analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D-E.

claim: ChIRP-seq on day 4 mES-iN identified 14975 peaks called by MACS, and the peak signals are consistent between replicates (n = 4) with little signal in RNase-treated control samples.
source: There are 14975 peaks called by MACS, and the peak signals are consistent between replicates (n = 4) with little signal in RNase-treated control samples (Figure 4B).
evidence: ChIRP-seq analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: 1092 high confidence lnc-Nr2f1 binding peaks were obtained after filtering for the most significant and reproducible binding events.
source: We obtained 1092 high confidence peaks with further filtering for the most significant and reproducible binding events (see Materials and methods for filtering criteria).
evidence: ChIRP-seq peak filtering analysis.

claim: Lnc-Nr2f1 binds to the intronic region of Nrp2, a gene with known roles in neuronal pathfinding.
source: As an example, lnc-Nr2f1 binds to the intronic region of Nrp2, a gene with known roles in neuronal pathfinding (Figure 4C).
evidence: ChIRP-seq data shown in Figure 4C with reference to known gene function.

claim: GREAT analysis associated the 1092 lnc-Nr2f1 binding sites to 1534 genes.
source: To understand which gene ontology terms are enriched in the genes adjacent to the mES-iN ChIRP peaks, we performed GREAT analysis and associated the 1092 lnc-Nr2f1 binding sites to 1534 genes.
evidence: GREAT analysis of ChIRP-seq peaks.

claim: GO term analysis of genes adjacent to lnc-Nr2f1 binding sites revealed enrichment for neuronal terms such as central nervous system development, synapse organization and chemical synaptic transmission.
source: GO term analysis revealed that these genes that enriched for neuronal terms such as central nervous system development, synapse organization and chemical synaptic transmission (Figure 4D).
evidence: Gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Lnc-Nr2f1 binding sites showed significant enrichments co-localizing with enhancers, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 marks relative to the background.
source: Using the publicly available ChIP-seq peak sets for CTCF, enhancer, H3K27ac, H3K4me3 and PolII obtained from mouse adult cortex and E14.5 brain, we found significant enrichments of those peaks co-localizing with the enhancers, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 marks relatively to the background (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D) (Shen et al., 2012).
evidence: Overlap analysis with public ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: DNA motif analysis of lnc-Nr2f1 binding sites revealed several basic helix loop helix (bHLH) factor motifs that are significantly enriched (NeuroD1, Atoh1, Olig2 and Ptf1a).
source: DNA motif analysis of lnc-Nr2f1 binding sites revealed several basic helix loop helix (bHLH) factor motifs that are significantly enriched (NeuroD1, Atoh1, Olig2 and Ptf1a) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: 3.2% and 13.2% lncNr2f1 ChIRP-seq peaks overlapped with Ngn2 and Ascl1 ChIP peaks, respectively.
source: We found that direct overlap between lncNr2f1 ChIRP-seq peaks and ChIP-seq peaks are low but statistically significant. 3.2% and 13.2% lncNr2f1 ChIRP-seq peaks overlapped with Ngn2 and Ascl1 ChIP peaks, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Overlap analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claim: LncNr2f1 target genes overlap very significantly with Ngn2 (37.9%) or Ascl1 (67.3%) target genes.
source: For peak-associated genes, lncNr2f1 target genes overlap very significantly with Ngn2 (37.9%) or Ascl1 (67.3%) target genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Gene-level overlap analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G.

claim: 177 common genes were found between the 1534 genes adjacent to the mouse lnc-Nr2f1 ChIRP peaks and the genes up or downregulated upon lnc-Nr2f1 overexpression (p<0.0001, Chi Square).
source: To understand whether the lnc-Nr2f1 regulates the genes listed in Figure 3E, we overlapped the 1534 genes adjacent to the mouse lnc-Nr2f1 ChIRP peaks with the genes up or downregulated upon lnc-Nr2f1 overexpression, we found 177 common genes between the two lists (p<0.0001, Chi Square), suggesting that those genes might be direct lnc-Nr2f1 targets since they are occupied by lnc-Nr2f1 RNA and are significantly altered when manipulating lnc-Nr2f1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: Statistical overlap analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The long human lnc-NR2F1 isoform two significantly increased the proportion of TauEGFP cells with projections, albeit with a slight smaller magnitude than the mouse lncRNA.
source: The long human lnc-NR2F1 isoform two significantly increased the proportion of TauEGFP cells with projections, albeit with a slight smaller magnitude than the mouse lncRNA.
evidence: Morphological quantification in neuronal reprogramming assay.

claim: Long lnc-NR2F1 isoform one inhibited neuronal maturation while the short isoform three had no significant effect.
source: Intriguingly, long isoform one inhibited neuronal maturation while the short isoform three had no significant effect (Figure 5B).
evidence: Morphological quantification shown in Figure 5B.

claim: There are approximately 10-fold more genomic occupancy for the long vs. short isoform of lnc-NR2F1: 4404 ChIRP-seq peaks for exon 11 (n = 4) vs. 415 ChIRP-seq peaks for exon 7 (n = 4), respectively.
source: There are approximately 10-fold more genomic occupancy for the long vs. short isoform of lnc-NR2F1: 4404 ChIRP-seq peaks for exon 11 (n = 4) vs. 415 ChIRP-seq peaks for exon 7 (n = 4), respectively.
evidence: ChIRP-seq peak calling analysis.

claim: Genomic occupancy sites of different lnc-NR2F1 exons showed limited overlap of peaks.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis of domain specific chromatin localization, genomic occupancy sites of different lnc-NR2F1 exons showed limited overlap of peaks (Figure 5C), suggesting that the long- and short- specific exon might be each binding to different genomic loci and regulating different subsets of downstream genes.
evidence: ChIRP-seq peak overlap analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The shortest isoform, human lnc-NR2F1 isoform 3, had the lowest number of differentially regulated genes (5 downregulated and four upregulated) compared to isoform 1 (1147 downregulated and 414 upregulated) and isoform 2 (141 downregulated and 45 upregulated).
source: We then assessed the transcriptional response which the three isoforms of human lnc-NR2F1 varied quantitatively: The shortest isoform, human lnc-NR2F1 isoform 3, had the lowest number of differentially regulated genes (5 downregulated and four upregulated) compared to isoform 1 (1147 downregulated and 414 upregulated) and isoform 2 (141 downregulated and 45 upregulated) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F.

claim: 913 high confidence peaks were obtained for long-isoform domain ChIRP and no peaks for short-isoform domain ChIRP after filtering.
source: After further filtering the peaks for high confidence peaks, we obtained 913 high confidence peaks for long-isoform domain ChIRP and no peaks for short-isoform domain ChIRP (see Materials and methods for filtering criteria).
evidence: ChIRP-seq peak filtering analysis.

claim: Relative to the human genome, the long isoform-specific peaks are more enriched in the exonic, intronic, enhancer and promoter regions and depleted in the intergenic regions.
source: Relative to the human genome, the long isoform-specific peaks are more enriched in the exonic, intronic, enhancer and promoter regions and depleted in the intergenic regions (Figure 5E).
evidence: Genomic distribution analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Lnc-NR2F1 ChIRP peaks are enriched in promoter, enhancer, and transcribed regions, compared to the whole genome which majority is in the quiescent state.
source: Furthermore, ChIRP peaks are characterized by chromatin state model, which defines human genome with 25 chromatin states using 12 biochemical features (histone modifications, DNA accessibility, DNA methylation, RNA-seq and other epigenetic signals) (Matsui et al., 2012). Lnc-NR2F1 ChIRP peaks are enriched in promoter, enhancer, and transcribed regions, compared to the whole genome which majority is in the quiescent state (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: ChromHMM analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D with citation to chromatin state model.

claim: The 1361 high confidence peak associated genes by the long isoform-specific domain ChIRP are all enriched for neuronal specific biological terms such central nervous system development, cell-cell adhesion and regulation of nervous system development.
source: The 1361 high confidence peak associated genes by the long isoform-specific domain ChIRP are all enriched for neuronal specific biological terms such central nervous system development, cell-cell adhesion and regulation of nervous system development (Figure 5F).
evidence: Gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 5F.

claim: There is a significant overlap between the genes adjacent to peaks from the long isoform-specific domain ChIRP and the genes adjacent to the mouse lnc-Nr2f1 ChIRP (207 genes overlapped, Chi-square test, p<0.0001).
source: There is also a significant overlap between the genes adjacent to peaks from the long isoform-specific domain ChIRP and the genes adjacent to the mouse lnc-Nr2f1 ChIRP, indicating a possible conserved functions of lnc-Nr2f1 between mouse and human (207 genes overlapped, Chi-square test, p<0.0001) (Figure 5G).
evidence: Statistical overlap analysis shown in Figure 5G.

claim: There is a significant overlap between the genes adjacent to the peaks from the long isoform-specific domain ChIRP and the autism risk genes (114 genes, Chi-square test, p<0.0001).
source: We also observed a significant overlap between the genes adjacent to the peaks from the long isoform-specific domain ChIRP and the autism risk genes (114 genes, Chi-square test, p<0.0001) (Figure 5H).
evidence: Statistical overlap analysis shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Peaks of long isoform-specific exon 11 ChIRP are enriched for multiple basic-helix-loop-helix motifs (Ascl1, NeuroD1, Olig2 and Atoh1) which all share the CANNTG motif.
source: Notably, peaks of long isoform-specific exon 11 ChIRP are enriched for multiple basic-helix-loop-helix motifs (Ascl1, NeuroD1, Olig2 and Atoh1) which all share the CANNTG motif (Kim et al., 2011) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E with citation to motif characterization.

claim: Direct lineage conversion by the transcription factors Brn2, Ascl1 and Myt1l (termed BAM factors in combination) into induced neuronal (iN) cells, recapitulates significant events controlling neurogenesis programs.
source: Direct lineage conversion by the transcription factors Brn2, Ascl1 and Myt1l (termed BAM factors in combination) into induced neuronal (iN) cells, recapitulates significant events controlling neurogenesis programs (Vierbuchen et al., 2010; Wapinski et al., 2013; Ang and Wernig, 2014), and therefore, it is a facile and informative system to study the role of lncRNAs in the establishment of neuronal identity.
evidence: Citations to published studies on iN cell reprogramming.

claim: Less than 2% of the genome encodes protein-coding genes.
source: Given that less than 2% of the genome encodes protein-coding genes, the majority of the genomic landscape is largely encompassed by non-coding elements.
evidence: Established knowledge about genome composition.

claim: Efforts to identify genetic variation linked to human disease through genome-wide association studies revealed a significant majority affecting the non-coding landscape.
source: Efforts to identify genetic variation linked to human disease through genome-wide association studies revealed a significant majority affecting the non-coding landscape.
evidence: General knowledge from GWAS studies.

claim: Despite recent findings that have greatly increased the number of protein coding genes implicated in human intellectual disability and autism, a majority of patients lack well-understood genetic lesions which include a large number of inherited variants occur in noncoding regions that could not be interpreted.
source: Nonetheless, despite recent findings that have greatly increased the number of protein coding genes implicated in human intellectual disability and autism, a majority of patients lack well-understood genetic lesions which include a large number of inherited variants occur in noncoding regions that could not be interpreted (Iossifov et al., 2014; Ronemus et al., 2014; Gilman et al., 2011; Iossifov et al., 2012; De Rubeis et al., 2014; O'Roak et al., 2012a; O'Roak et al., 2012b; Hormozdiari et al., 2015).
evidence: Citations to published studies on autism genetics.

claim: LncRNAs have been associated with human diseases primarily through alterations in expression levels.
source: LncRNAs have been associated with human diseases primarily through alterations in expression levels (Meng et al., 2015; Cheetham et al., 2013; Gupta et al., 2010).
evidence: Citations to published studies on lncRNA-disease associations.

claim: Chromosomal aberrations encompassing the lnc-NR2F1 locus and additional genes on chromosome 5q14 have been previously reported in several patients with neurodevelopmental deficits and congenital abnormalities.
source: Chromosomal aberrations encompassing the lnc-NR2F1 locus and additional genes on chromosome 5q14 have been previously reported in several patients with neurodevelopmental deficits and congenital abnormalities (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B and Supplementary file 1) (Al-Kateb et al., 2013; Brown et al., 2009; Cardoso et al., 2009; Malan et al., 2006).
evidence: Citations to published case reports shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The minimal deleted region across patients with structural variation encompassing the lnc-NR2F1 locus in the literature is approximately 230 kb, a small area encompassing the genes NR2F1 and lnc-NR2F1.
source: Across those patients with structural variation encompassing the lnc-NR2F1 locus in the literature, the minimal deleted region is approximately 230 kb, a small area encompassing the genes NR2F1 and lnc-NR2F1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Analysis of overlapping deletions from published cases shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The most notable overlapping phenotype across patients with lnc-NR2F1 locus deletions consists of global developmental delay, facial dysmorphism, and hearing loss.
source: The most notable overlapping phenotype consists of global developmental delay, facial dysmorphism, and hearing loss.
evidence: Synthesis of clinical features from multiple published cases.

claim: Hypotonia and opththalmological abnormalities are common diagnoses among patients with lnc-NR2F1 locus deletions.
source: Hypotonia and opththalmological abnormalities are also common diagnoses (Al-Kateb et al., 2013) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Citation to published case report and clinical data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Phenotypic heterogeneity amongst patients with lnc-NR2F1 locus deletions could be the result of dosage sensitive genes, polymorphisms on the unaffected allele, genomic variability, gender, and age, amongst others.
source: Phenotypic heterogeneity amongst patients could be the result of dosage sensitive genes, polymorphisms on the unaffected allele, genomic variability, gender, and age, amongst others.
evidence: Speculation about potential causes of phenotypic variability.

claim: It is possible that haploinsufficiency of lnc-NR2F1 is the primary cause for this syndrome and contribute to the phenotypes manifested across patients.
source: Given that lnc-NR2F1 is the only disrupted gene in this patient family, it is possible that haploinsufficiency is the primary cause for this syndrome and contribute to the phenotypes manifested across patients mentioned above.
evidence: Inference based on genetic data showing lnc-NR2F1 as only disrupted gene.

claim: Further studies including a larger sample size and independent cases are required to conclusively link lnc-NR2F1 mutations to multiple clinical symptoms.
source: Further studies including a larger sample size and independent cases are required to conclusively link lnc-NR2F1 mutations to multiple clinical symptoms described above.
evidence: Acknowledgment of limitations and need for additional studies.

claim: The father of the proband carries the same translocation and suffers from dyslexia and stuttering, suggesting that the phenotype may be transmitted in a Mendelian manner.
source: The father of the proband carries the same translocation and suffers from dyslexia and stuttering, suggesting that the phenotype may be transmitted in a Mendelian manner.
evidence: Inference from family pedigree data.

claim: The much milder phenotype of the father implies that additional genes, environmental factors, or compensatory neuronal circuitry acquired during adulthood may influence the severity of the outcome.
source: However, the much milder phenotype of the father implies that additional genes, environmental factors, or compensatory neuronal circuitry acquired during adulthood may influence the severity of the outcome.
evidence: Speculation based on phenotypic differences between father and son.

claim: Gain and loss of function studies as well as chromatin localization show that lnc-NR2F1 acts in trans to affect gene expression.
source: First, gain and loss of function studies as well as chromatin localization clearly show that lnc-NR2F1 acts in trans to affect gene expression.
evidence: Summary of experimental evidence from multiple assays.

claim: The phenotype of the lnc-Nr2f1 KO can be rescued by overexpression of lnc-Nr2f1 mRNA.
source: Second, we can rescue the phenotype of the lnc-Nr2f1 KO by overexpression of lnc-Nr2f1 mRNA.
evidence: Rescue experiment demonstrating specificity.

claim: Lnc-Nr2f1 overexpression in lnc-Nr2f1 KO cells does not affect Nr2f1 expression.
source: Third, lnc-Nr2f1 overexpression in lnc-Nr2f1 KO cells does not affect Nr2f1 expression.
evidence: Gene expression analysis showing independence of lncRNA and coding gene.

claim: ChIRP-sequencing of lnc-Nr2f1 in induced neurons derived from mES cells does not show binding of lnc-Nr2f1 in the Nr2f1 promoter region.
source: Fourth, ChIRP-sequencing of lnc-Nr2f1 in induced neurons derived from mES cells does not show binding of lnc-Nr2f1 in the Nr2f1 promoter region (Figure 4F).
evidence: ChIRP-seq data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Integrating human genetics and functional testing in neuronal lineage induction is a promising approach for discovering candidate lncRNAs involved in neurodevelopmental diseases.
source: Thus, integrating human genetics and functional testing in neuronal lineage induction is a promising approach for discovering candidate lncRNAs involved in neurodevelopmental diseases.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the overall study approach and results.

claim: Lnc-NR2F1 is an evolutionarily conserved lncRNA that functionally enhances induced neuronal cell maturation.
source: We further show that lnc-NR2F1 is an evolutionarily conserved lncRNA functionally enhances induced neuronal cell maturation and directly occupies and regulates transcription of neuronal genes including autism-associated genes.
evidence: Summary of conservation analysis and functional studies.

claim: Lnc-NR2F1 directly occupies and regulates transcription of neuronal genes including autism-associated genes.
source: We further show that lnc-NR2F1 is an evolutionarily conserved lncRNA functionally enhances induced neuronal cell maturation and directly occupies and regulates transcription of neuronal genes including autism-associated genes.
evidence: ChIRP-seq and RNA-seq data showing binding and regulation of autism genes.

claim: A t(5:12) chromosomal translocation in a family manifesting neurodevelopmental symptoms disrupts specifically lnc-NR2F1.
source: Here we find that a t(5:12) chromosomal translocation in a family manifesting neurodevelopmental symptoms disrupts specifically lnc-NR2F1.
evidence: Genetic analysis of patient CMS12200 and family.

claim: LncRNAs represent a new layer of complexity in the molecular architecture of the genome.
source: LncRNAs represent a new layer of complexity in the molecular architecture of the genome, and strategies to validate disease relevant lncRNAs are much needed.
evidence: General statement about lncRNA biology based on field knowledge.

claim: LncRNAs are widely expressed in the brain and may contribute to complex neurodevelopmental processes.
source: High-throughput analyses have shown that lncRNAs are widely expressed in the brain and may contribute to complex neurodevelopmental processes (Wapinski and Chang, 2011; Fertuzinhos et al., 2014; Valadkhan and Nilsen, 2010; Lv et al., 2013; Aprea et al., 2013; Ramos et al., 2013; Ramos et al., 2015; Ng et al., 2013).
evidence: Citations to published studies on lncRNA expression in brain.

claim: Few studies have examined the role of lncRNAs in brain development mostly due to technical difficulties.
source: However, few studies have examined the role of lncRNAs in brain development mostly due to technical difficulties.
evidence: Assessment of the state of the field.

claim: LncRNAs are emerging as critical regulators of diverse biological processes and have been increasingly associated with a wide range of diseases, based primarily on dysregulated expression.
source: However, lncRNAs are emerging as critical regulators of diverse biological processes and have been increasingly associated with a wide range of diseases, based primarily on dysregulated expression (Wapinski and Chang, 2011).
evidence: Citation to review on lncRNA function and disease association.

claim: Eukaryotic genomes are extensively transcribed to produce long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in a temporally and spatially regulated manner.
source: Eukaryotic genomes are extensively transcribed to produce long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in a temporally and spatially regulated manner (Flynn and Chang, 2014).
evidence: Citation to review on lncRNA transcription.

claim: LncRNAs were often dismissed as lacking functional relevance until recently.
source: Until recently, lncRNAs were often dismissed as lacking functional relevance.
evidence: Historical perspective on lncRNA field.
